text:
Carol likely wins because the seller’s misdescription of the car as a 1964 Thunderbird, reinforced by the misleading photo, breaches an express warranty that the car was a 1964 model, and the “as is” clause does not override that express description. The team note is incorrect: express warranty liability does not require proof of the seller’s carelessness or fault. Carol can likely recover damages or rescind the contract.
CONFIDENCE: 88
